portion_doctrine: Segments 1-10 of series_1_download.docx are a blog article from Resolve.com published Mar 27, 2026 titled '12 Common Invoice Payment Terms Every B2B Business Should Know.' Content is 80% boilerplate marketing/UI text, 20% real operational substance. The core value is a taxonomy of 12 payment term types with decision heuristics for each. No novel frameworks, no prompts, no proprietary methods. Actionable for pricing/terms selection only.
operating_rules: Set payment terms early: How much they owe, when they need to pay, and how they can pay must be explicit on every invoice
Match industry norms: Construction uses Net 60-90; retail suppliers use Net 30; SaaS/professional services use Net 15-30 or upfront
New clients start conservative: Short terms (Net 7-15) or partial upfront payment (CBS 25-50%) until relationship matures
Large orders warrant credit assessment before extending long terms (Net 60-90)
Use early-pay discounts (2/10 Net 30) as a primary tool to accelerate cash flow without straining relationships
Include late-payment penalties and interest invoices (1.5% monthly example given) to discourage chronic non-payment
For subscription/repeat clients, use Cash on Next Delivery (CND) to create predictable payment rhythm
named_methods: Cash account: No credit, immediate payment only (retail/small transactions)
Cash Before Shipment (CBS): 25-50% down before shipping (custom work, designers, furniture makers)
Cash in Advance (CIA): Full payment before work begins (high-value projects, first-time clients)
Cash on Next Delivery (CND): Full payment before next scheduled delivery (subscription/repeat-order businesses)
Cash on Delivery (COD): Payment due when customer receives goods (wholesale distribution, local delivery)
Cash with Order (CWO): Full payment before production begins (manufacturing, sourcing scenarios)
Contra Payment: Offset mutual debts in services/products instead of cash (mutual trading relationships)
End of Month (EOM): Payment due last day of invoice month, optionally combined with days (EOM+30)
Interest Invoice: Separate invoice for late fees/interest on overdue amounts (critical for chronic late payers)
Terms of Sale: Full transaction details (due date, amount, quantity, delivery, payment methods, taxes, return policies)
Net 7/10/30/60/90: Standard credit term in days after invoice date (Net 30 is B2B default across most industries)
2/10 Net 30: 2% discount if paid in 10 days; full amount due in 30 days (common variations: 3/15 Net 60, 5/10 Net 30)
numbers: 25% of small businesses experience payment delays up to 30 days beyond agreed terms
60% of invoices paid late across the US (US EXIM Bank statistic)
25-50% down payment typical for CBS (custom work scenario)
Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): early-pay discounts can significantly reduce this metric
1.5% monthly interest rate example on late invoices
15% restocking fee example for returns (example invoice)
2% discount for 10-day payment; 3% for 15-day; 5% for 10-day (variations given)
Net 30 is the B2B standard across most industries
Under $1,000 invoices work best with Net 15 or due upon receipt
$10,000+ may need Net 60-90 with credit evaluation
specific_tactics: Batch-process invoices with EOM terms to align with monthly accounting cycles (APteams efficiency gain)
Stage payments for large projects (construction/phased work): partial payments tied to project milestones
Forward dating: Push invoice date back to after delivery to give buyer more time
MFI (Month Following Invoice): Payment due on specific date in following month (e.g., 15 MFI = 15th of next month)
1MD (One Month's Debit): Single payment covering entire month's supply at billing cycle end
Due Upon Receipt: For smaller jobs, repairs, service calls
Use early-pay discounts as competitive advantage for attracting new buyers (online markets)
Always include preferred B2B payment methods on invoice (ACH, credit card, wire transfer)
Use credit checks before extending net terms to new customers
Combine partial upfront (CBS) with follow-up net terms as trust builds (CIA → Net terms progression)
gates: Credit assessment gate: Required before extending Net 60+ to new customers
Payment method diversity gate: Invoice must specify accepted payment methods (ACH, credit card, wire transfer, check)

weird_gold: Contra payment (offset mutual debts in services/products) is underutilized for trading relationships; could be strategic for barter-economy plays
1MD (One Month's Debit) is not widely known but critical for recurring/subscription-based suppliers
Forward dating is a simple lever for buyer accommodation without changing cash flow impact (just timing perception)
Interest invoices as a separate line item can be more effective than annual late-payment penalties (psychological impact of seeing the fee itemized)
